topic.title: Representation Geometry and Neural Generalization
topic.overview: Why can two networks fit their training data equally well yet behave differently on new examples? This topic studies the geometry of learned representations, including kernel spectra, intrinsic dimension, activation structure, and alignment. Its central distinction is between the ability to optimize a model and the usefulness of the representation that optimization produces.
topic.whyItMatters: Representation measurements can reveal weaknesses that parameter counts or training accuracy conceal. Their interpretation depends on whether a result concerns idealized infinite-width networks, a particular training regime, or diagnostics applied after a finite model has already been trained.
topic.evolution: The 1993 population-coding work uses description length to learn economical internal codes. A 2020 analysis separates trainability from generalization through neural tangent kernel spectra. Later representatives examine feature-learning dynamics and neural collapse; a 2026 study relates post-hoc generalization bounds to embedding dimension and downstream sensitivity. These are complementary explanations at different levels of abstraction.
openQuestions: Which representation diagnostics predict failures before deployment?
When do infinite-width conclusions describe networks that learn substantially changing features?

papers.title: Spherization Layer: Representation Using Only Angles
papers.tldr: The spherization layer learns information-preserving representations on a hypersphere so that information is expressed through angles.

papers.title: Stochastic Adaptive Activation Function
papers.tldr: Adaptive SwisH adjusts activation behavior to unit position and input context, with reported accuracy and convergence benefits across multiple tasks.

papers.title: Towards Disentangling Information Paths with Coded ResNeXt
papers.tldr: Coded ResNeXt assigns classes predefined information paths that support smaller standalone classifiers and early predictions while improving reported accuracy.

papers.title: Towards Understanding the Mixture-of-Experts Layer in Deep Learning
papers.tldr: For a structured classification problem, the paper proves that learned routing lets multiple nonlinear experts solve tasks that challenge a single expert.

papers.title: Transform Once: Efficient Operator Learning in Frequency Domain
papers.tldr: Transform Once learns directly in frequency space, reducing repeated-transform costs while improving accuracy in the reported dynamics experiments.

papers.title: A Toy Model of Universality: Reverse Engineering how Networks Learn Group Operations
papers.tldr: Small networks learning group operations share an interpretable algorithmic family, but their precise circuits and learning order vary.

papers.title: Are Neurons Actually Collapsed? On the Fine-Grained Structure in Neural Representations
papers.tldr: Small variations beneath apparent neural collapse can retain enough input structure to recover classes never supplied as training labels.

papers.title: Data Representations’ Study of Latent Image Manifolds
papers.tldr: Image classifiers exhibit characteristic changes in representation curvature across layers, with final-layer curvature differences correlated with generalization.

papers.title: Defects of Convolutional Decoder Networks in Frequency Representation
papers.tldr: Frequency-domain analysis proves three representation defects involving high-frequency weakening, repeated spectral signals, and difficulty learning shifted frequencies.

papers.title: Emergence of Sparse Representations from Noise
papers.tldr: Training networks to handle noise introduces implicit loss terms that produce sparse, specialised neurons and potentially more interpretable representations.

papers.title: Feature learning in deep classifiers through Intermediate Neural Collapse
papers.tldr: An empirical study finds increasingly class-organized representations across network depth and alignment between upper-layer class means and dominant weight directions.

papers.title: Fundamental Limits of Two-layer Autoencoders, and Achieving Them with Gradient Methods
papers.tldr: The paper characterizes optimal nonlinear two-layer autoencoders for Gaussian data and shows that gradient methods reach those solutions.

papers.title: HarsanyiNet: Computing Accurate Shapley Values in a Single Forward Propagation
papers.tldr: HarsanyiNet is designed to compute predictions and exact input Shapley values together in one forward pass.

papers.title: Linear CNNs Discover the Statistical Structure of the Dataset Using Only the Most Dominant Frequencies
papers.tldr: A theory of linear CNNs links staged learning and dominant-frequency bias to interactions between dataset structure and convolutional architecture.

papers.title: Mechanistic Mode Connectivity
papers.tldr: The paper connects loss-landscape geometry to predictive mechanisms and proposes fine-tuning designed to alter reliance on spurious attributes.

papers.title: Neural networks trained with SGD learn distributions of increasing complexity
papers.tldr: The study finds that SGD-trained networks use lower-order input statistics early and exploit higher-order structure later in training.

papers.title: Nonlinear Advantage: Trained Networks Might Not Be As Complex as You Think
papers.tldr: Experiments show that many nonlinear units can be removed after training while preserving high performance, although early removal is more damaging.

papers.title: Polarity Is All You Need to Learn and Transfer Faster
papers.tldr: Adequately chosen weight polarities can reduce learning time and data needs, although preset polarities can also be disadvantageous.

papers.title: Spherical Inducing Features for Orthogonally-Decoupled Gaussian Processes
papers.tldr: Spherical features in an orthogonally decomposed Gaussian process improve representation flexibility and scalability in the proposed approximation framework.

papers.title: The Hessian perspective into the Nature of Convolutional Neural Networks
papers.tldr: A Toeplitz-based analysis yields tight Hessian-rank bounds for linear-activation CNNs and supports square-root scaling with parameter count.

papers.title: What Can Be Learnt With Wide Convolutional Neural Networks?
papers.tldr: Infinite-width convolutional networks benefit from local low-dimensional targets, but hierarchical structure alone does not ensure efficient high-dimensional learning.

papers.title: What do CNNs Learn in the First Layer and Why? A Linear Systems Perspective
papers.tldr: A linear-systems analysis explains consistent first-layer CNN energy profiles through image-patch statistics and fits the approximate whitening observed in ResNet and VGG.

papers.title: A Spectral Theory of Neural Prediction and Alignment
papers.tldr: A spectral decomposition explains how different neural-network representations can achieve similarly accurate predictions of brain activity.

papers.title: An Inductive Bias for Tabular Deep Learning
papers.tldr: A lightweight layer encourages smoother feature representations and improves neural network performance and convergence on 14 tabular datasets.

papers.title: Deep learning with kernels through RKHM and the Perron-Frobenius operator
papers.tldr: Deep RKHM combines generalized kernel spaces and composition operators to analyze deep kernel models, including generalization and benign overfitting.

papers.title: Deep Neural Collapse Is Provably Optimal for the Deep Unconstrained Features Model
papers.tldr: For binary classification in a deep unconstrained features model, the authors prove that the unique global optimum exhibits deep neural collapse.

papers.title: Diffused Redundancy in Pre-trained Representations
papers.tldr: Pretrained layers often distribute useful information redundantly, allowing sufficiently large random neuron subsets to retain substantial downstream performance.

papers.title: GEQ: Gaussian Kernel Inspired Equilibrium Models
papers.tldr: GEQ introduces Gaussian kernels into equilibrium models to capture nonlinear features and improve performance and stability over OptEqs.

papers.title: Going Beyond Linear Mode Connectivity: The Layerwise Linear Feature Connectivity
papers.tldr: Networks with low-loss linear parameter connections also show linear feature connections in nearly all layers across the studied settings.

papers.title: High-dimensional Asymptotics of Denoising Autoencoders
papers.tldr: A high-dimensional analysis derives denoising test error and quantifies the benefit of a skip connection in a two-layer nonlinear autoencoder.

papers.title: High dimensional, tabular deep learning with an auxiliary knowledge graph
papers.tldr: PLATO uses a knowledge graph of input features to regularize neural-network weights for tabular datasets with many features and few samples.

papers.title: Improving Compositional Generalization using Iterated Learning and Simplicial Embeddings
papers.tldr: Iterated learning with approximately discrete simplicial embeddings improves generalization to unseen combinations in vision and molecular graph tasks.

papers.title: Inner Product-based Neural Network Similarity
papers.tldr: With shared filter-decomposition coefficients, cosine distances between filter atoms provide an efficient proxy for neural-network representational similarity.

papers.title: Learning Curves for Deep Structured Gaussian Feature Models
papers.tldr: An analysis of deep Gaussian-feature models finds that first-layer weight correlations can help generalisation, while later-layer structure is generally detrimental.

papers.title: Neural Sculpting: Uncovering hierarchically modular task structure in neural networks through pruning and network analysis
papers.tldr: Neural Sculpting combines pruning and network analysis to reveal hierarchical subfunctions in learned Boolean and MNIST-based tasks.

papers.title: Neural (Tangent Kernel) Collapse
papers.tldr: Under a class-aligned block structure in the neural tangent kernel, the paper proves neural collapse for mean-squared-error training.

papers.title: Polyhedron Attention Module: Learning Adaptive-order Interactions
papers.tldr: PAM builds piecewise polynomial models whose feature-interaction orders adapt to different regions of the input space.

papers.title: Provable Advantage of Curriculum Learning on Parity Targets with Mixed Inputs
papers.tldr: For a specified mixed-input parity-learning regime, sparse-first curriculum training provably needs fewer steps than noisy gradient descent on unordered samples.

papers.title: Provable Guarantees for Nonlinear Feature Learning in Three-Layer Neural Networks
papers.tldr: The paper proves that three-layer networks can efficiently learn nonlinear features that yield advantages over two-layer networks in specified settings.

papers.title: Residual Alignment: Uncovering the Mechanisms of Residual Networks
papers.tldr: Measurements reveal coordinated residual transformations and nearly linear representation paths in tested well-generalizing ResNets, with supporting proof in a proposed mathematical model.

papers.title: Robust Learning with Progressive Data Expansion Against Spurious Correlation
papers.tldr: Progressive Data Expansion starts with balanced groups and gradually adds data to improve worst-group performance against spurious correlations.

papers.title: Sampling weights of deep neural networks
papers.tldr: Data-dependent sampling constructs neural networks without iterative internal-parameter training, with approximation guarantees and large empirical construction-speed gains.

papers.title: Scaling MLPs: A Tale of Inductive Bias
papers.tldr: Scaled MLPs improve substantially on vision tasks and broadly mirror modern networks, providing evidence about inductive bias and theoretical proxies.

papers.title: Simplicity Bias in 1-Hidden Layer Neural Networks
papers.tldr: The paper formalizes simplicity bias through low-dimensional input dependence and uses feature-diverse ensembles to improve robustness to Gaussian noise.

papers.title: SmoothHess: ReLU Network Feature Interactions via Stein's Lemma
papers.tldr: SmoothHess estimates feature interactions in Gaussian-smoothed ReLU networks using gradient samples and Stein’s lemma.

papers.title: The Tunnel Effect: Building Data Representations in Deep Neural Networks
papers.tldr: Deep image classifiers can develop a later-layer tunnel that compresses already separable representations and degrades out-of-distribution generalization.

papers.title: Theoretical Analysis of the Inductive Biases in Deep Convolutional Networks
papers.tldr: The paper proves CNN approximation and sample-efficiency results and separates the learning benefits of locality and weight sharing.

papers.title: Towards the Difficulty for a Deep Neural Network to Learn Concepts of Different Complexities
papers.tldr: The paper theoretically connects greater learning difficulty to concepts that require interactions among more input variables.

papers.title: A Theory of Non-Linear Feature Learning with One Gradient Step in Two-Layer Neural Networks
papers.tldr: With a learning rate that grows with sample size, one gradient step can create useful nonlinear features in the two-layer networks studied.

papers.title: Amortized Variational Deep Kernel Learning
papers.tldr: Sharing parameters between inducing-point amortization and deep kernel learning helps prevent spurious correlations and improves results across several evaluated tasks.

papers.title: Asymptotics of Learning with Deep Structured (Random) Features
papers.tldr: The paper characterizes readout test error through feature covariance in a proportional high-dimensional limit, including structured random deep networks.

papers.title: BiSHop: Bi-Directional Cellular Learning for Tabular Data with Generalized Sparse Modern Hopfield Model
papers.tldr: BiSHop combines row-wise and column-wise learning with adaptive sparse Hopfield layers to improve tabular prediction and reduce tuning effort.

papers.title: Complexity Matters: Feature Learning in the Presence of Spurious Correlations
papers.tldr: Controlled experiments and theory show how spurious-feature complexity and correlation strength affect core-feature learning and the assumptions behind debiasing methods.

papers.title: Deep Regression Representation Learning with Topology
papers.tldr: PH-Reg improves regression representations by encouraging their dimension and topology to match the target space.

papers.title: Don’t trust your eyes: on the (un)reliability of feature visualizations
papers.tldr: Feature visualizations can be disconnected from natural-input behavior, and the paper identifies empirical and theoretical reasons to question their reliability.

papers.title: Feature Contamination: Neural Networks Learn Uncorrelated Features and Fail to Generalize
papers.tldr: The paper identifies feature contamination, where learning uncorrelated features alongside predictive ones can undermine generalization under distribution shifts.

papers.title: Generalized Neural Collapse for a Large Number of Classes
papers.tldr: The paper extends neural collapse to many-class settings, finding margin-maximizing geometry empirically and proving it under specified model conditions.

papers.title: Generalizing Orthogonalization for Models with Non-Linearities
papers.tldr: The paper extends orthogonalization methods to nonlinear models and demonstrates corrections for sensitive information, metadata, and unwanted embedding attributes.

papers.title: Grokking Group Multiplication with Cosets
papers.tldr: The authors reverse engineer small networks performing permutation-group arithmetic and find circuits organized around genuine subgroup structure.

papers.title: How Deep Networks Learn Sparse and Hierarchical Data: the Sparse Random Hierarchy Model
papers.tldr: A sparse hierarchical data model connects learning abstract representations with learning transformation insensitivity and characterizes CNN sample requirements.

papers.title: Initial Guessing Bias: How Untrained Networks Favor Some Classes
papers.tldr: Network architecture and preprocessing can make an untrained classifier assign every input to one class, even without explicit biases.

papers.title: Is Kernel Prediction More Powerful than Gating in Convolutional Neural Networks?
papers.tldr: Gating combined with fixed-weight layers can express weight prediction, and the reformulation reduces memory in a denoising application.

papers.title: Layerwise Change of Knowledge in Neural Networks
papers.tldr: An extended interaction framework tracks which inference patterns emerge and disappear across a neural network’s layers.

papers.title: On the Emergence of Cross-Task Linearity in Pretraining-Finetuning Paradigm
papers.tldr: Models fine-tuned from a shared checkpoint often show approximately linear feature changes when their weights are interpolated.

papers.title: On the Nonlinearity of Layer Normalization
papers.tldr: Layer normalization supplies substantial representational nonlinearity, and grouping can amplify it under the paper's stated assumption.

papers.title: Position: Tensor Networks are a Valuable Asset for Green AI
papers.tldr: This position paper argues that tensor networks' mathematical structure and compression potential make them valuable candidates for sustainable, inclusive AI research.

papers.title: Position: The No Free Lunch Theorem, Kolmogorov Complexity, and the Role of Inductive Biases in Machine Learning
papers.tldr: The paper argues that shared preferences for low-complexity data help explain broad neural-model usefulness despite no free lunch theorems.

papers.title: Position: The Platonic Representation Hypothesis
papers.tldr: The paper argues that model representations are converging and hypothesizes a shared statistical representation of reality.

papers.title: ReLUs Are Sufficient for Learning Implicit Neural Representations
papers.tldr: Wavelet-inspired constraints enable ReLU-only networks to learn state-of-the-art implicit representations and support principled analysis of function regularity.

papers.title: Simplicity Bias of Two-Layer Networks beyond Linearly Separable Data
papers.tldr: Under small initialization and gradient flow, two-layer networks develop clustered features, with results suggesting intermediate representations may transfer better.

papers.title: Sliding Down the Stairs: How Correlated Latent Variables Accelerate Learning with Neural Networks
papers.tldr: Correlations between latent variables can accelerate SGD’s recovery of features encoded in higher-order input statistics.

papers.title: Sparse and Structured Hopfield Networks
papers.tldr: A loss-based framework unifies sparse Hopfield memory retrieval and extends it to retrieving structured associations among patterns.

papers.title: Tilting the Odds at the Lottery: the Interplay of Overparameterisation and Curricula in Neural Networks
papers.tldr: A theoretical two-layer-network analysis shows that strong overparameterization can reduce the additional benefit of curriculum learning.

papers.title: Understanding MLP-Mixer as a wide and sparse MLP
papers.tldr: The paper explains MLP-Mixer as a wider, structured sparse MLP and connects its performance to architectural sparsity.

papers.title: When Representations Align: Universality in Representation Learning Dynamics
papers.tldr: An effective theory explains shared aspects of representation learning dynamics when neural architectures are sufficiently flexible.

papers.title: Which Frequencies do CNNs Need? Emergent Bottleneck Structure in Feature Learning
papers.tldr: The paper links near-minimal parameter norms in CNNs to frequency bottlenecks, with an additional stability assumption for activation-level results.

papers.title: A Functional Extension of Semi-Structured Networks
papers.tldr: The paper extends semi-structured networks to functional data, combining interpretable feature effects with flexible neural modeling and improved scalability.

papers.title: Addressing Spectral Bias of Deep Neural Networks by Multi-Grade Deep Learning
papers.tldr: Training shallow networks in successive grades helps their compositions capture high-frequency information that deep networks often struggle to learn.

papers.title: Amortized Eigendecomposition for Neural Networks

papers.title: An exactly solvable model for emergence and scaling laws in the multitask sparse parity problem
papers.tldr: An exactly solvable skill-based model captures emergence and loss scaling in neural networks trained on multitask sparse parity.

papers.title: Average gradient outer product as a mechanism for deep neural collapse
papers.tldr: The paper establishes an AGOP-based mechanism for neural collapse in Deep Recursive Feature Machines and finds supporting evidence in broader neural networks.

papers.title: $C^2M^3$: Cycle-Consistent Multi-Model Merging
papers.tldr: C²M³ merges networks without data by aligning neurons coherently across layers and enforcing consistent mappings among multiple models.

papers.title: Counter-Current Learning: A Biologically Plausible Dual Network Approach for Deep Learning
papers.tldr: Counter-current learning trains interacting input and target networks through opposing signal flows as a biologically inspired credit-assignment mechanism.

papers.title: Deep Learning Through A Telescoping Lens: A Simple Model Provides Empirical Insights On Grokking, Gradient Boosting & Beyond
papers.tldr: A telescoping model built from first-order approximations provides empirical tools for understanding surprising neural-network behavior.

papers.title: Dendritic Integration Inspired Artificial Neural Networks Capture Data Correlation

papers.title: DeNetDM: Debiasing by Network Depth Modulation
papers.tldr: DeNetDM uses network depth to separate biased and debiased learning, improving robustness without bias annotations or explicit data augmentation.

papers.title: Dual-Perspective Activation: Efficient Channel Denoising via Joint Forward-Backward Criterion for Artificial Neural Networks
papers.tldr: DPA uses forward and backward propagation signals to suppress irrelevant channels without adding parameters.

papers.title: Exploring and Exploiting the Asymmetric Valley of Deep Neural Networks
papers.tldr: Parameter sign consistency helps explain asymmetric loss valleys and is associated with how effectively separately trained models can be combined.

papers.title: Get rich quick: exact solutions reveal how unbalanced initializations promote rapid feature learning
papers.tldr: Exact analyses and experiments show how layer imbalances can accelerate nonlinear feature learning, while revealing a different requirement in linear networks.

papers.title: Identifying Functionally Important Features with End-to-End Sparse Dictionary Learning
papers.tldr: Training sparse autoencoders to preserve model outputs produces more compact, functionally relevant feature dictionaries without a reported loss of interpretability.

papers.title: Infinite-Dimensional Feature Interaction

papers.title: Nonparametric Classification on Low Dimensional Manifolds using Overparameterized Convolutional Residual Networks
papers.tldr: Under smoothness and low-dimensional manifold assumptions, weight-decayed ConvResNeXts adapt efficiently while implicitly selecting a sparse set of blocks.

papers.title: Set-based Neural Network Encoding Without Weight Tying

papers.title: The Impact of Geometric Complexity on Neural Collapse in Transfer Learning

papers.title: Towards the Dynamics of a DNN Learning Symbolic Interactions

papers.title: Understanding Visual Feature Reliance through the Lens of Complexity

papers.title: Unveiling The Matthew Effect Across Channels: Assessing Layer Width Sufficiency via Weight Norm Variance
papers.tldr: Patterns in channel weight-norm variance indicate layer-width sufficiency and guide CNN width changes that reduce parameters while improving reported performance.

papers.title: What Variables Affect Out-of-Distribution Generalization in Pretrained Models?
papers.tldr: Experiments show that harmful representation compression in deep layers is not universal and is reduced by high-resolution training data with many classes.

papers.title: Approximating Latent Manifolds in Neural Networks via Vanishing Ideals
papers.tldr: Polynomial descriptions of learned class manifolds let the authors replace network layers while preserving comparable accuracy and improving efficiency.

papers.title: Dimension-Independent Rates for Structured Neural Density Estimation
papers.tldr: Under local conditional dependence assumptions, neural density estimators can achieve convergence rates governed by neighborhood size rather than total data dimension.

papers.title: Eigenspectrum Analysis of Neural Networks without Aspect Ratio Bias
papers.tldr: FARMS uses fixed-aspect-ratio submatrices to reduce bias in spectral diagnostics and improve their use in training and pruning.

papers.title: Feature Learning beyond the Lazy-Rich Dichotomy: Insights from Representational Geometry
papers.tldr: Tracking the geometry of task-relevant representations reveals learning stages and strategies that the lazy–rich distinction misses.

papers.title: Feature learning from non-Gaussian inputs: the case of Independent Component Analysis in high dimensions
papers.tldr: An ICA analysis shows how optimization choices and non-Gaussian data structure jointly determine the sample requirements of feature learning.

papers.title: From Kernels to Features: A Multi-Scale Adaptive Theory of Feature Learning
papers.tldr: A multi-scale theory connects kernel rescaling and directional adaptation while identifying feature-learning effects that rescaling alone misses.

papers.title: Inducing, Detecting and Characterising Neural Modules: A Pipeline for Functional Interpretability in Reinforcement Learning
papers.tldr: A pipeline encourages, detects, and experimentally validates functional navigation modules in reinforcement learning policy networks.

papers.title: Inductive Gradient Adjustment for Spectral Bias in Implicit Neural Representations
papers.tldr: IGA uses kernel-informed gradient transformations to adjust spectral bias and improve textures and edges in implicit neural representations.

papers.title: Learning Input Encodings for Kernel-Optimal Implicit Neural Representations
papers.tldr: Infinite-width kernel analysis motivates a regularizer and learnable input encodings for principled implicit neural representation design.

papers.title: NEAR: Neural Electromagnetic Array Response
papers.tldr: NEAR uses an untrained, physics-informed neural representation to reconstruct radar responses from sparse measurements and adapt to unseen environments.

papers.title: Not all solutions are created equal: An analytical dissociation of functional and representational similarity in deep linear neural networks
papers.tldr: Network representations and functions can vary independently, while robustness to parameter noise constrains representations toward the task.

papers.title: Position: A Theory of Deep Learning Must Include Compositional Sparsity
papers.tldr: The authors argue that deep-learning theory must explain how networks exploit functions built from low-dimensional components.

papers.title: Position: Algebra Unveils Deep Learning - An Invitation to Neuroalgebraic Geometry
papers.tldr: The paper proposes algebraic geometry as a framework for connecting neural-network function spaces with fundamental learning behavior.

papers.title: Position: Deep Learning is Not So Mysterious or Different
papers.tldr: The paper argues that established generalization theory and soft preferences for simpler solutions explain several supposedly mysterious deep learning behaviors.

papers.title: Position: Not All Explanations for Deep Learning Phenomena Are Equally Valuable
papers.tldr: Surprising deep-learning phenomena are most useful when they help refine broad theories rather than only receive isolated explanations.

papers.title: Tensor Product Neural Networks for Functional ANOVA Model
papers.tldr: ANOVA-TPNN guarantees a unique functional decomposition and produces more stable component-based interpretations.

papers.title: The Complexity of Learning Sparse Superposed Features with Feedback
papers.tldr: The paper bounds the comparison feedback needed to recover sparse hidden features, with guarantees that depend on the agent's access to activations.

papers.title: Understanding Nonlinear Implicit Bias via Region Counts in Input Space
papers.tldr: Counting connected prediction regions offers a function-based measure of implicit bias that correlates with simpler boundaries and better generalization.

papers.title: A Closer Look at NTK Alignment: Linking Phase Transitions in Deep Image Regression
papers.tldr: An NTK-based analysis connects three changes in SIREN image reconstruction training, revealing a shared account of their learning dynamics.

papers.title: Better NTK Conditioning: A Free Lunch from (ReLU) Nonlinear Activation in Wide Neural Networks
papers.tldr: In wide networks, ReLU improves gradient-feature separation and neural tangent kernel conditioning, implying better worst-case optimization rates.

papers.title: From Flat to Hierarchical: Extracting Sparse Representations with Matching Pursuit
papers.tldr: MP-SAE uses sequential residual-guided encoding to recover hierarchical and nonlinearly accessible features that existing sparse autoencoders can miss.

papers.title: Hybrid Autoencoders for Tabular Data: Leveraging Model-Based Augmentation in Low-Label Settings
papers.tldr: A tree-guided hybrid autoencoder improves neural representations for tabular tasks with few labels while using only the neural encoder at inference.

papers.title: Neural Collapse in Cumulative Link Models for Ordinal Regression: An Analysis with Unconstrained Feature Model
papers.tldr: Under an Unconstrained Feature Model with fixed thresholds, ordinal regression exhibits class collapse and a one-dimensional geometry respecting category order.

papers.title: On Linear Mode Connectivity of Mixture-of-Experts Architectures
papers.tldr: A symmetry-aware matching algorithm reveals low-loss linear connections between independently trained mixture-of-experts models across diverse evaluated configurations.

papers.title: On the Expressive Power of Mixture-of-Experts for Structured Complex Tasks
papers.tldr: The paper proves efficient mixture-of-experts approximation results for functions with low-dimensional or compositionally sparse structure.

papers.title: On the VC dimension of deep group convolutional neural networks
papers.tldr: The paper derives VC-dimension bounds for deep ReLU group convolutional networks, examining dependence on architecture and input resolution.

papers.title: Projecting Assumptions: The Duality Between Sparse Autoencoders and Concept Geometry
papers.tldr: Sparse autoencoder architectures impose assumptions about concept geometry that determine which concepts they can recover.

papers.title: Scaling can lead to compositional generalization
papers.tldr: Scaling data and models can yield compositional generalization when training sufficiently covers the task space, with linear decoding revealing relevant internal structure.

papers.title: Shortcut Features as Top Eigenfunctions of NTK: A Linear Neural Network Case and More
papers.tldr: An NTK analysis links shortcut learning in linear networks to dominant eigenfunctions, with supporting empirical patterns in more complex networks.

papers.title: Sinusoidal Initialization, Time for a New Start

papers.title: The Computational Advantage of Depth in Learning High-Dimensional Hierarchical Targets
papers.tldr: For a controlled class of hierarchical targets, the paper proves that deep feature learning successively reduces effective dimension and sample requirements.

papers.title: Uncovering a Universal Abstract Algorithm for Modular Addition in Neural Networks
papers.tldr: The paper identifies an approximate Chinese Remainder Theorem algorithm underlying neural modular addition and explains its compact feature requirements.

papers.title: Understanding Bias Terms in Neural Representations

papers.title: A Fourier perspective on the learning dynamics of neural networks: from sample complexities to mechanistic insights
papers.tldr: Fourier analysis shows how image amplitude structure can accelerate learning of phase information even without directly helping classification.

papers.title: A Theory of How Pretraining Shapes Inductive Bias in Fine-Tuning
papers.tldr: A theory of diagonal linear networks identifies how initialization controls feature reuse and refinement during fine-tuning.

papers.title: A unified theory of feature learning in RNNs and DNNs

papers.title: Activation with Intrinsic-Extrinsic Consensus
papers.tldr: AIEC suppresses irrelevant neural-network channels by combining evidence from their activation statistics and learned decision weights.

papers.title: Batch Normalization for Neural Networks on Complex Domains

papers.title: Beyond Structural Symmetries: Linear Mode Connectivity via Neuron Identifiability

papers.title: CauchyNet: Compact and Data-Efficient Learning using Holomorphic Activation Functions

papers.title: Credit Assignment via Neural Manifold Noise Correlation

papers.title: Dataset Distillation Efficiently Encodes Low-Dimensional Representations from Gradient-Based Learning of Non-Linear Tasks

papers.title: Deep Learning of Compositional Targets with Hierarchical Spectral Methods

papers.title: Deep Networks Learn Deep Hierarchical Models

papers.title: Deep Neural Network Regression with Functional Covariates

papers.title: Deep neural networks divide and conquer dihedral multiplication

papers.title: Do Neural Operators Forget Geometry? The Forgetting Hypothesis in Deep Operator Learning

papers.title: Grokking Finite-Dimensional Algebra
papers.tldr: A finite-dimensional algebra framework connects grokking to multiplication structure, matrix factorization, and learned representations beyond group operations.

papers.title: Local Intrinsic Dimension of Representations Predicts Alignment and Generalization in AI Models and Human Brain
papers.tldr: Lower local intrinsic dimension is associated with better generalization and stronger representational alignment across AI models and human brain activity.

papers.title: Low-dimensional topology of deep neural networks

papers.title: On the Expressive Power of Permutation-Equivariant Weight-Space Networks

papers.title: Optimizing Rank for High-Fidelity Implicit Neural Representations

papers.title: Quantifying and Optimizing Simplicity via Polynomial Representations

papers.title: Query Lens: Interpreting Sparse Key-Value Features with Indirect Effects

papers.title: Revisiting the Platonic Representation Hypothesis: An Aristotelian View

papers.title: Robustness of Mixtures of Experts to Feature Noise
papers.tldr: With equal parameter counts and latent modular inputs, sparse expert activation filters feature noise and improves robustness and convergence.

papers.title: Sequential Group Composition: A Window into the Mechanics of Deep Learning
papers.tldr: Sequential group composition reveals how encoding shapes shallow-network learning and how architectures exploiting associativity can greatly improve sequence-length scaling.

papers.title: Understanding Generalization from Embedding Dimension and Distributional Convergence
papers.tldr: A post-training generalization bound connects embedding dimension and prediction sensitivity to the gap between held-out and population risk.

papers.title: Unifying Low Dimensional Spectra in Deep Learning
papers.tldr: An unconstrained-feature analysis links low-dimensional spectra across weights, gradients, and Hessians to the geometry of deep neural collapse.

papers.title: Who Said Neural Networks Aren’t Linear?
papers.tldr: Linearizers make structured neural mappings linear in induced vector spaces, enabling algebraic composition, single-step diffusion sampling, and projective generative models.
